Commentary.Commentary: We are back with England's reply! The umpires and players are all out in the middle. Davina Perrin and Olivia Brinsden are the openers for England Women Under-19. Fatima Khan will start the proceedings for Pakistan with the ball. Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Amuruthaa Surenkumar was the star with the ball for England, picking up three crucial wickets, while Olivia Brinsden, Eve O'Neill and Tilly Corteen-Coleman chipped in with two each to their names. However, a lot of the credit belongs to wicketkeeper Katie Jones, who was an absolute livewire behind the stumps. With five dismissals to her name, her contributions don’t fully capture just how exceptional she was throughout the innings. With just 67 runs to chase, England will fancy their chances of wrapping this up comfortably. That said, spin could play a key role and potentially turn this into another low-scoring thriller. Stick around to see how it all unfolds!

Amuruthaa Surenkumar is in for a chat. She says that the conditions were pretty good for bowling. Tells that the plan was to try and attack the stumps. Mentions that this World Cup experience will put her in good stead for her playing career back home.

From a steady 18/0, they suffered a stunning collapse, slipping to 41/7, undone by disciplined bowling, exceptional fielding from England, and their own poor shot selection and misjudged running between the wickets. Toward the end, Quratulain and Memoona Khalid put together a small but meaningful partnership that helped Pakistan scrape together a total they could at least fight for.

Pakistan’s openers started cautiously but soon found their rhythm, getting the scoreboard ticking nicely. However, the momentum shifted dramatically when Amuruthaa Surenkumar was introduced into the attack. She struck twice in consecutive deliveries, dismissing Fatima Khan and Ravail Farhan, and Pakistan never managed to recover from there.

A dismal batting display from Pakistan Women Under-19 sees them bowled out for just 66 runs. It was an exceptional performance from the England Women Under-19, both with the ball and in the field, as they dominated the innings from start to finish.

OUT! STUMPED! Katie Jones has stamped her authority on the innings with some brilliant glove work, and fittingly, she has the final say to wrap things up. Tilly Corteen-Coleman slows it down and drags the length back, on middle and leg, Shahar Bano gets out in front to swipe it away. She fails to connect as she is beaten in the flight. The ball slides past the bat and the keeper Katie Jones moves to her left to gather it before whipping the bails off. It is referred upstairs and the replays show that Bano was out of her crease when the bails were removed by Jones. Pakistan have been bowled out for 66!

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is down in the middle. She says that it is a lovely afternoon with a bit of cloud cover. Reckons that it will be important for pacers to pitch it up. Adds that batters should look to play it late and right under their eyes.

The 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup in Johor has gotten off to a damp start, with rain forcing the first two games to be abandoned without a result. As a new day dawns, better fortunes are hoped for as England take on Pakistan at the Johor Cricket Academy Oval in a Group B clash. England began their campaign by posting a competitive 144 in their opening game, with valuable contributions from Davina Perrin, Charlotte Stubbs, Jemima Spence, and Charlotte Lambert. The bowlers struck early to claim two Irish wickets, but rain ended the game after just 4.2 overs of Ireland's chase, leaving much of England’s bowling unit untested. Erin Thomas and Abigale Norgrove had a quiet outing with the bat and will be eager to make an impact against Pakistan. On the other hand, Pakistan had an even more frustrating start, with their game against the USA abandoned without a ball being bowled. The Asian side has not had a particularly great build-up to the tournament, having failed to make the Super Fours of the Asia Cup last year after suffering defeats to India and Nepal. In their warmup fixtures, Pakistan endured a comprehensive loss to Australia before registering a convincing win over Nigeria in their final practice match. In the batting department, Areesha Ansari and Komal Khan have shown glimpses of promise and will be pivotal to Pakistan's chances in this tournament. On the bowling front, the seam duo of Fatima Khan and Mahnoor Zeb will be key with the new ball. Against a strong English side, Pakistan will need to be at their absolute best to make a statement. These two sides last met in the 2023 edition of the World Cup, where England secured a resounding victory. Can Pakistan rise to the occasion and deliver a statement performance against their Group B rivals? We shall find out.
